authors: Hawkins TS, Baskin CC, Baskin JM
title: Morphophysiological dormancy in seeds of three eastern North American Sanicula species (Apiaceae subf. Saniculoideae): evolutionary implications for dormancy break
why: Germination study of three Sanicula species from the Baskin lab, whose methods usually incubate seeds in light and in darkness; the full text may give a light versus dark germination result for the genus (sense_light_nonvisual, carried to Sanicula crassicaulis as g). The abstract seen mentions only warm and cold stratification.

title: Effect of day length on germination of seeds collected in Alaska
why: Abstract gives long-day-only germination for leatherleaf (logged in sweep-35 from the abstract, partial); the full text gives the percentages and day lengths, upgrading the record to full text, and may cover other Alaskan species on the plant list.

title: Some characteristics of the eye and the electroretinogram of the prairie dog
why: Prairie dog eye and ERG study cited by Jacobs, Neitz and Crognale 1985 (10.1007/BF00613974); ERG work of this kind usually reports flicker following (cff_hz) and may give eye dimensions useful for acuity in Cynomys.
get: journal via library (Elsevier, Experimental Neurology back file)

title: Anatomical evidence for cone and rod-like receptors in the gray squirrel, ground squirrel, and prairie dog retinas
why: Retinal anatomy of the prairie dog, cited by Jacobs et al 1985; gives the receptor types (cones and rod-like receptors) and may give cone classes, closing receptor_classes for Cynomys; its companion Green and Dowling 1975 (J Comp Neurol 159:461-472) gives the electrophysiology.
